source.title: Biblia Sacra Vulgata, Clementine edition (1592)
source.attribution: Biblia Sacra Vulgata, editio Clementina (1592), public domain. USFX text from seven1m/open-bibles, held by the Vetus V0 app.
source.provenance: Taken verse by verse from vetus-v0/data/vulgate/lat-clementine.usfx.xml (SHA-256 5da5f3c07fa6896d4a2b45f5f309c3ece43e554fd059b31b8ae3688bbd182baf) by scripts/corpus-la-build.mts; nothing was retyped. Clementine spelling kept (ae ligatures as printed, i/j and u/v as printed, no macrons). One verse is one sentence (the verse is not split, although it may hold several clauses or sentences), so every sentence is addressable by its reference. The Vulgate numbers this psalm 22 (Greek/Vulgate numbering); the references here use the Hebrew number 23 so that they line up with the other languages’ Psalm 23. The text has not been compared with a second, independent edition.
source.licenseNote: The Clementine Vulgate (1592) is in the public domain. The USFX file comes from seven1m/open-bibles (Bible texts that are public domain or openly licensed).
source.modifications: none: each sentence is exactly one verse of the source (surrounding whitespace trimmed).

review.notes: Wording verified by byte-comparison against the Clementine USFX file it was copied from (a copy-integrity check, not a second edition).

english.source: World English Bible (public domain), eBible.org eng-web, copied verbatim from the German/Hindi corpora for the verses they carry

sentences.text: Psalmus David. Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit :
sentences.english: Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.

sentences.text: in loco pascuæ, ibi me collocavit. Super aquam refectionis educavit me ;
sentences.english: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.

sentences.text: animam meam convertit. Deduxit me super semitas justitiæ propter nomen suum.
sentences.english: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

sentences.text: Nam etsi ambulavero in medio umbræ mortis, non timebo mala, quoniam tu mecum es. Virga tua, et baculus tuus, ipsa me consolata sunt.
sentences.english: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.

sentences.text: Parasti in conspectu meo mensam adversus eos qui tribulant me ; impinguasti in oleo caput meum : et calix meus inebrians, quam præclarus est !
sentences.english: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.

sentences.text: Et misericordia tua subsequetur me omnibus diebus vitæ meæ ; et ut inhabitem in domo Domini in longitudinem dierum.
sentences.english: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.
